chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Describe to me the believer. He (peace be upon him) said: [The believer is] strength in religion, firmness in gentleness, faith in conviction, eagerness in jurisprudence, activity in guidance, piety in uprightness, knowledge in forbearance, gratitude in gentleness, generosity in truth, moderation in wealth, composure in poverty, pardon in ability, obedience in sincerity, piety in desire, eagerness in jihad, prayer in busyness, and patience in hardship. In shaking disasters, he is solemn; in misfortunes, he is patient; in prosperity, he is thankful. He does not backbite, nor does he become arrogant, nor does he sever kinship ties. He is not weak, nor harsh, nor coarse. His arrogance does not outrun him, his stomach does not disgrace him, and his genital desire does not overpower him. He does not envy people, nor does he stint, nor does he squander, nor does he exceed bounds. He supports the oppressed and has mercy on the poor. His self is in distress because of him, while people are at ease from him. He does not desire the world, nor does he fear the humiliation of people. For people, there is a concern they have turned to, and for him, there is a concern that occupies him. No deficiency is seen in his forbearance, no weakness in his opinion, and no waste in his religion. He guides whoever consults him and helps whoever helps him, and he refrains from falsehood, coarse speech, and ignorance. These are the attributes of the believer.
ai.seo_question: What are the key moral and spiritual attributes of a true believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) describes the ideal believer as possessing a balanced character where strength is coupled with gentleness, and faith with conviction. The believer is characterized by moral integrity, social responsibility, and spiritual discipline, avoiding arrogance, envy, and excess while supporting the oppressed and seeking God's pleasure over worldly concerns.
